unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision keeps the clear channel and the unknown ocean. It cuts the father's task (the slave-power) and the bitter consequence that the sons would 'pay for the pilotage' with lives or wasted energies. The first draft had kept both.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The 1840–1870 / 1870–1900 generational contrast still implies that the old pilotage will not serve.

evidence.quote: he might be content to let his sons pay for the pilotage; and it mattered little to his success whether they paid it with their lives wasted on battle-fields

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the sentence 'The task done, he might be content to let his sons pay for the pilotage; and it mattered little...' before the generations sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Plan essential: 'Pilotage: the father's channel was clear, the sons faced an unknown ocean.' The cost clause is not required but carries the point.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The image becomes a neutral contrast instead of an indictment of what the father's success cost his sons. That indictment is the chapter's link between inheritance and failed education.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Pilotage loses the cost borne by the sons

unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The European middle-class parallel and 'The boy naturally took for granted that this sort of world was the world which he was to fit' survive.

evidence.quote: He could not be convinced that moral standards had nothing to do with it, and that utilitarian morality was good enough for him, as it was for the graceless.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'He could not be convinced...' sentence after 'So they were.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Plan essential: 'The Puritan resists change, believing his standards higher; "So they were."' The reversal that follows is integral to that unit.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The dry concession was meant to be followed by the Puritan's error: the issue was not morality at all. Without it, the reasoning about why the Puritan could not take the new stamp is lost, and the passage reads as simple endorsement of the old standards.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Puritan argument loses its corrective turn after 'So they were'

compelled to learn by memory a quantity of things that did not amuse him.
